rss.title: datasette-leaflet 0.3
rss.summary: Release: datasette-leaflet 0.3 OpenStreetMap have a very reasonable policy that hits to their hosted tile server should send a referrer header . Datasette table pages used the Referrer-Policy: no-referrer HTTP header, causing plugins that loaded tiles from OpenStreetMap to violate that policy. datasette-leaflet is the plugin that loads a bundled Leaflet so other Datasette plugins can depend on it. It now sets the referrer policy on the tile requests themselves to strict-origin-when-cross-origin , passing the host but not the full path to the page. Tags: leaflet , datasette , openstreetmap

rss.title: AI Ambition: ArtCraft Cloned Photoshop and Now Wants to "Rebuild Everything"
rss.summary: ArtCraft used AI to rewrite Photoshop as open source software. For CEO Brandon Thomas, the vision is even bigger: to take back the internet!
rss.text_excerpt:
The theme of day two of the AI Engineer Code Summit in San Francisco was increasing ambition using AI . And there have been few projects as ambitious as ArtCraft in the AI era. So far the fledgling company has released 17 open source versions of popular software tools , starting with a Photoshop alternative built from scratch in Rust called PhotoCraft . You could feel the excitement in the room this morning when ArtCraft founder and CEO Brandon Thomas presented a kind of manifesto for AI-based open source at AIE Code. When he mentioned that ArtCraft had cloned Adobe’s Acrobat, with a product called PdfCraft, it got a round of applause from the audience. In wrapping up, his rallying cries of “let's take back the entire internet” and “let's rebuild everything” were greeted with whoops and cheers. Thomas began his presentation by reliving the internet’s early history. In his view, the web started out with the right intentions, but things got screwed up once Web 2.0 hit the mainstream. “We had a bunch of chat applications that were completely open,” he said, regarding the 1990s internet. “So, IRC is like Discord, but you can spin up your own servers that you actually own. You can use whatever programs to automate them and interrogate them without rules.” His point wasn’t necessarily that everything was open source, but that web users could freely build things. With Flash, for example — a commercial animation tool eventually acquired by Adobe — “kids were making all kinds of animations.” When Web 2.0 came along, with its superior broadband and smartphones, “it brought everybody into the fold.” Thomas acknowledged that this widened the scope of internet software, but at the cost of that freedom to build with leading apps. “The diffuse, experimental, early web started to disappear,” he said. “The APIs got taken away from us, and then we started seeing distribution being gatekept by the big providers.” It seems Adobe in particular annoyed Thomas. He described getting billed with an unexpected fee when he cancelled a monthly plan. “It's really frustrating that the web — that was once really, really promising and open and free — has turned into this extractive, owned, rent-seeking world.” This inspired him to start ArtCraft, “with the ethos of ‘let's build everything open source.’” A message even anti-AI people have gotten behind, according to Thomas. rss.title: Anthropic's IPO roadshow video
rss.summary: Anthropic's IPO roadshow video Anthropic kicked off their IPO roadshow yesterday, and their roadshow video has some previously unreleased information about how their business works. The section on "Approach to compute" with co-founder Tom Brown is particularly interesting, describing how Anthropic train and serve Claude across AWS Trainium, Google TPUs, NVIDIA GPUs, and AMD GPUs. I'm not sure why there's no official video transcript, but here's one that I extracted using MacWhisper. Highlights below: We train and serve Claude now across all four major chip families. That's only possible because early on we made an unconventional bet on a multi-chip strategy. At the time, many people thought that running AI models on different chips wasn't worth the effort. Each chip needs its own tailored software stack and inference stack, which is expensive and difficult to build. We've now been doing it for years, and we've gotten incredibly good at it. [...] As an example, this year, we started working with AMD GPUs for the first time. In the past, bringing on a new chip platform took dozens of engineers months of work This time, we had Mythos try it out. It got Claude running on AMD in just three days, with basically no human intervention . Claude ported or wrote almost 100% of the kernels. [...] The second driver of our compute advantage is our rate of discovery of compute multipliers. We focus on total effective compute, which is the multiplicative product of physical capacity times the compute multipliers that we discover. Each one we discover makes our pool of total effective compute bigger. For example, say you need 100 units of compute to train a model of a certain intelligence. A 4x compute multiplier means you can use 25 units of compute to train the exact same model. Or you can use those hundred physical units to train an even more intelligent model that would have previously required 400 units. Compute multipliers create a competitive advantage for us that's hard to replicate. They build on each other. Each new multiplier we discover has a positive effect on the multipliers before it. They stack. We believe that this can accelerate even further as we approach recursive self-improvement. Claude will be able to discover compute multipliers entirely by itself , allowing the number of compute multipliers to grow faster and faster. We got a hint at Anthropic's multi-chip strategy last September in their postmortem of three recent issues , where they described bugs that affected just their TPU deployments. # Paxeer X Network Paxeer X Network is a distributed HyperState Machine for payments, code execution and intent routing, developed by Sidiora Labs. The LayerX kernel is the core of the network and runs inside every `paxd` node. It executes each transaction when it arrives, assigns the next position in one global sequence and returns a signed execution receipt before any block is voted. It builds every block: the proposed block is the sealed sequence, with the signed sequence batch first and the executed transactions behind it in sequence order. Validators check that batch and the pinned proposer, replay the block and commit it; they do not select or order transactions. `paxd` uses EVM chain identifier **125** (`0x7d`) and native token **PAX**. ## Overview Atrex Kernel Agent (AKA) optimizes GPU kernels through an iterative loop of research, implementation, profiling, and evaluation. Coding agents propose candidates; the Supervisor verifies correctness and performance before promoting an improvement. Its lightweight workflow keeps the optimization loop focused, while a plugin architecture lets users configure and replace agents, workspaces, evaluation, execution, and knowledge providers. AKA supports Claude, Qoder, Codex, Pi, and [DSH](docs/dsh-harness-adapter.md), with CUDA, Triton, CuTeDSL, FlyDSL, and TileLang tooling for supported NVIDIA, AMD, and T-Head PPU environments. It is for reverse engineers, security reviewers, and anyone auditing a shipped Flutter app who has hit the wall where most tools stop at ARM64 assembly. Flutter compiles Dart ahead of time. There is no bytecode and no reflection metadata, so teams ship banking, fintech, health and identity logic on the assumption that AOT hides it. It does not. The public toolchain is simply fragmented, version-fragile, and stops at assembly. **The rule that shapes everything here: Jadart never prints a confident guess.** An instruction it does not model prints as raw arm64. A call argument it cannot reconstruct prints `(...)`. A field whose name is not in the binary prints `field_0x8`. A Dart release whose format is not registered raises a typed error instead of parsing with a grammar that might be wrong. # Division Swarm

**The operating system for autonomous multi-agent systems.** Swarm runs fleets of LLM agents as a durable, stateful system. You declare it in YAML and a deterministic engine runs it, owning state, routing, isolation, cost, and recovery. The LLM never runs the system: agents reason in scoped sessions and emit events, and deterministic code, never the model, decides what each result changes. More than a simple orchestrator that decides which agent runs next, Swarm runs the system around it. Work is modeled as entities (an order, a ticket, a candidate business) moving through a state machine you declare: the runtime schedules hundreds at once, keeps them isolated, meters their spend, persists their state, and resumes them after a crash, days later if a timer or a human kept them waiting. Any run can be replayed or forked from the log. Deterministic routing is one piece; the rest is the operating system. Single Go binary, local/dev SQLite by default with Postgres as a production opt-in. # LingoFuse > **分布式系统地基。跨语言、跨进程、跨机器；同时支撑后台与前台。** > > 不写 IDL，不生成桩代码，不搭 HTTP 服务。任何语言写的函数，任何其他语言都能直接调。 > > **定位**：LingoFuse 不只是"跨语言 RPC"——它是**前沿型程序的多应用组合体系**与**多物理硬件组合体系**的通讯底座，也是**多语言团队生态互补的协作底座**。 [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT) [![Languages](https://img.shields.io/badge/languages-18%20first--party%20%2B%2030%20via%20tools-blue)]() [![Latency](https://img.shields.io/badge/same--machine%20IPC-%3C1ms-brightgreen)]() > **作者的话**：LingoFuse 是我自己用的框架，顺手 MIT 开源。它没有融资目标、没有商业化路线、没有社区运营计划——开源的目的就是**帮助所有人**，没有别的。它的底层内核是从**单日 PB 级真实流量**中洗礼出来的，不是实验室里拼出来的。它在地球上没有竞品、没有前例，所以它能做出别人做不出的架构——甚至 AI + 人类组合也无法低成本复制的架构。分支项目（pasAgent-v3、cppAgent 等）会过时，但 LF 作为地基不会。星标少、人气低，但请不要被现象蒙蔽——它是真正的成长型项目，只要世界科技圈有个浪头，它就能起飞。详见下方[项目性质](#项目性质自用开源无目的分享本身)。 --- ## 你现在在哪 如果你是第一次打开这个仓库，建议按下面的顺序往下读——每一步只花几分钟，读完就能判断自己该继续深入，还是直接换个方案。 1. **[这是什么](#这是什么)** — 三分钟讲清 LingoFuse 到底解决什么问题 2. **[使用门槛](#使用门槛这是黑科技不是开箱即用)** — 说实话：它不适合所有人，你得先确认自己是不是目标用户 3. **[为什么需要它](#为什么需要它)** — 和 gRPC / REST / 消息队列比，它到底不同在哪 4. **[快速开始](#快速开始)** — Windows 上最短的上手路径，不需要编译任何东西 5. **[语言支持](#语言支持)** — 挑一种你最熟悉的语言，进入对应目录继续 如果你已经决定要用了，可以直接跳到[语言支持](#语言支持)或[快速开始](#快速开始)。如果你想理解内部机制，从[技术短文 · 内核与应用](#技术短文--内核与应用)那 17 篇短文里挑一篇看——它们每一篇都独立可读；更完整的机制知识库在 [Z.LingoFuse.md](Z.LingoFuse.md)。如果你是团队负责人，先看[多语言团队协作策略](#多语言团队协作策略)和[项目性质](#项目性质自用开源无目的分享本身)。 --- ## 这是什么 LingoFuse 是一个**分布式系统地基**。 大多数人第一次听到"跨语言 RPC"，想到的是 gRPC、REST、HTTP POST——这些方案解决的是"**A 进程调 B 进程的一个函数**"，这是**点对点**问题。LingoFuse 解决的不是这个，它解决的是"**多个进程、多台机器、多种硬件、多种语言、多种应用，如何组合成一个可运行的系统**"。 换句话说，它同时为两面提供地基： - **分布式后台地基**：服务器、后台服务、AI Agent 后端、计算节点、存储节点之间如何互相发现、路由、负载均衡、断线重连、稳定会话。后台之间可以是同语言，也可以是异语言；可以同机，也可以跨机、跨 IDC。 - **分布式前台地基**：客户端、Agent 前端、设备端、浏览器、移动端、嵌入式如何接入这个系统——通过原生 FFI（桌面/移动/嵌入式）或 HTTP 桥接（浏览器/受限设备）。前台可以是一台机器，也可以是几万台设备。 跨语言、跨进程、跨机器，是它的**技术手段**，不是定位本身。真正的定位是：**让"分布式组合"成为默认能力，而不是需要额外搭建的基础设施。** 为什么叫"地基"而不是"框架"？因为框架规定你盖什么楼，地基不规定——但它保证你盖什么楼都不会塌。而且地基是从真实生产流量中长出来的（见下方[项目性质](#项目性质自用开源无目的分享本身)），不是设计出来的。 ### 它想解决的两类 AI 时代组合问题 LingoFuse 真正要解决的问题，是 AI 时代正在成形的两类组合问题： **多应用组合**——一个系统不再是一个巨型应用，而是**多个 Agent / 多个应用 / 多个服务**的组合。写代码的 Agent、查数据的 Agent、做计算的 Agent、调硬件接口的 Agent，用不同语言写成，跑在不同机器上，需要互相调用、互相协作、有状态隔离、有故障隔离。LingoFuse 让它们之间的通讯像同进程函数调用一样简单——不需要为每一种组合写网关、写 IDL、写桩代码。 **多物理硬件组合**——一个系统不再是一台机器，而是**多台机器、多种硬件、多种算力**的组合。GPU 节点做推理，CPU 集群做数据处理，嵌入式设备做采集，工作站做可视化。它们需要被组合成一个统一的计算池，按任务分发、按负载路由、按数据形态传输（二进制帧、视频帧、矩阵、张量）。LingoFuse 的 C4 网格、P2P 负载、序列化族、二进制句柄就是为这个场
